demo_prompts.label: Simple factual recall
demo_prompts.user: What is the capital of Japan?
demo_prompts.why: Short prompt — TTFT 233ms → 150ms (−35.5%). Artemis small_prompt_v1 sequential, P50 over 50 runs.

</think>

optimized.text:
<think>
The user wants to know Japan's capital. That's straightforward — it's Tokyo, which became the capital in 1869 when Emperor Meiji moved the imperial seat from Kyoto. Tokyo remains the capital today.
</think>

Japan's capital is **Tokyo**. It has served as the seat of government since 1869, when Emperor Meiji relocated the imperial court from Kyoto.

demo_prompts.label: Long-context extraction
demo_prompts.user:
The United States Constitution, drafted in 1787 and ratified in 1788, established the framework of the federal government. The Constitutional Convention was held in Philadelphia from May to September 1787. Delegates from twelve of the thirteen states attended. Among the most influential delegates was James Madison of Virginia, who arrived with a detailed plan for a new government known as the Virginia Plan. Madison had spent months studying historical republics and confederacies in preparation. His meticulous notes from the Convention provide the most complete record of the proceedings. Due to his central role in drafting the document and shaping its provisions, Madison became known as the Father of the Constitution, though he himself was modest about the title.

According to the passage above about the U.S. Constitution and the Constitutional Convention, who is known as the "Father of the Constitution" and played a principal role in its drafting at the Constitutional Convention in 1787?
demo_prompts.why: Long-context prefill — TTFT 1341ms → 779ms (−41.9%). Artemis long_context_v1 sequential, P50 over 50 runs. Biggest TTFT win across all scenarios.
